ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, the line segment $AD=21\,cm$, point $B$ is on line segment $AD$, $C$ is the midpoint of $BD$, and $AB=\frac{1}{3}CD$, what is the length of $BC$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Let $AB=x$, then $CD=3x$,\\
since C is the midpoint of BD,\\
thus $BC=CD=3x$,\\
therefore $3x+3x+x=21$,\\
solving this equation yields $x=3$,\\
$BC=3\times 3=\boxed{9}$ cm.

method.method_draft: First read the diagram as a straight segment with points ordered A-B-C-D, so AD is composed of AB plus BD, and BD is split at C into BC and CD. From the text, AD=21 cm, C is the midpoint of BD, and AB=(1/3)CD. Let BD be the main unknown. Because C is the midpoint of BD, CD=BD/2 and BC=BD/2. Then AB=(1/3)(BD/2)=BD/6. Use the whole length AD=AB+BD, so 21=BD/6+BD=(7/6)BD. Solve BD=18, hence BC=BD/2=9 cm.
